sections.html: Carroll County sits in central Maryland on the Piedmont Plateau, with Pennsylvania to the north and Howard, Baltimore and Frederick counties around the rest. Westminster is the county seat and Eldersburg the largest community. The 2020 census counted 172,891 residents, with a 2025 estimate of 176,677. The terrain is rolling hills and forest, and the housing ranges from older downtown Westminster homes to newer subdivisions around Eldersburg. Most residents drive, since Westminster has no inter-county bus or rail service toward Baltimore County. Route 140 is the main road.

The county rate is $1.018 per $100 of assessed value and the state adds $0.112, for $1.130 per $100 outside any town. Towns add their own rates, so where you live changes your bill more than most owners expect. Confirm figures with the local government before you rely on them.

Between January 1, 2023 and January 1, 2026, residential full cash value climbed 16.1%. A higher value is spread across three equal steps, and a lower one applies right away. For an owner-occupied home the homestead credit limits yearly growth in taxable value, at 5% in unincorporated areas, while each town sets its own cap, listed beside its rate above.

Appeals start with the state's local assessment office, which for Carroll is at 15 East Main Street in Westminster. Plan on a first deadline of 45 days from the notice date.

A full-year payment and the first half of a split bill both come due July 1, and neither collects interest until after September 30. The second half is due December 1 and stays interest-free through December 31.

Paying the year in one check earns a discount of 1% by July 31 or 0.5% by August 31. Splitting the bill earns nothing, and the second half picks up a service charge unless both halves are paid by September 30.

  • Full-year and first-installment bills become delinquent on October 1.
  • The second installment becomes delinquent January 1.
  • Interest and penalties are not waived for any reason, and due dates are not extended.
  • A pending appeal or tax credit application does not change the due date.
  • A bill that never arrives does not excuse nonpayment, so request a duplicate.

Check your current bill for any changes to these dates.

Each June the county auctions liens on unpaid real estate tax in an online sale through RealAuction, with proceedings starting around April 1.

From May 1, delinquent taxes must be paid by cash, certified check or money order, and additional fees apply, so owners who wait until late April or May lose the card and online options. Paying the current year does not shield you from legal action over unpaid prior years. The Collections Office links a Homeowner Protection Program page, so ask about eligibility if the sale is close.

sections.h2: How to pay and who to call
sections.html:
The Collections Office is on the first floor of the county building at 225 N. Center Street, Westminster. Hours are Monday through Thursday 8 am to 5 pm and Friday 8 am to 3 pm. The phone number is 410-386-2971.

  • Online or by phone with a card: a vendor fee applies, 2.5% on cards and $1.50 for an e-check.
  • By mail: PO Box 3237, Westminster, MD 21158-3237.
  • Drop box: open around the clock in the lower parking lot outside the building.
  • Cash or check: accepted at Carroll County Public Library branches.

Credits worth asking about include the Senior Tax Credit for homeowners 65 and older, a $15,000 assessment exemption for legally blind owners and a full exemption for owners with a 100% service-connected permanent disability. Qualifications differ, so call before assuming you are eligible.

sections.h2: Reading the town table before you list
sections.html:
Where the house sits decides the combined rate. Two houses with the same assessment can have very different bills if one is in Westminster at $1.6900 and the other in Mount Airy at $1.3262. A buyer's lender and agent will run the numbers by address, so know yours before you price the house. The homestead cap works the same way: it ranges from 3% in Mount Airy to 10% in Sykesville and Taneytown, and a cap only helps an owner who lives there and has applied for the credit.

If you rent the house out or it sits empty, the cap may not apply to you, and the buyer's bill could be higher or lower than yours depending on how they use it.

sections.h2: Planning a closing around the installments
sections.html:
Carroll's schedule gives sellers a few clear checkpoints. Before October 1 a full-year or first-installment bill is still interest-free. After that date it is delinquent, and a second installment turns delinquent January 1. Because the county does not waive interest or extend due dates, a closing that falls close to one of those dates should have the payment confirmed in writing by the Collections Office.

If you are selling before the year's taxes are fully paid, the title company will usually collect the unpaid portion from the proceeds. Tell your lender if taxes are escrowed, since the escrow account may already have paid part of the bill. Ask for a payoff that covers any lien and the days between your request and the closing date.

A seller who has been in the house for years may already hold a credit that will not carry over to the buyer. The county's Senior Tax Credit serves homeowners 65 and older, and a $15,000 assessment exemption is available to legally blind owners. An owner with a 100% service-connected permanent disability can qualify for a full exemption. The state credit and the Homeowner Protection Program add further options. Because each one has its own rules and paperwork, call the Collections Office at 410-386-2971 before you assume you still qualify, and mention the sale date when you do.

Westminster averages about 43 inches of precipitation and 20 inches of snow a year, so roofs, gutters and heating systems work hard. Buyers touring an older downtown house will check those first, so keep records of any recent roof or furnace work.

1. Pull the bill and find out which installment, if any, is unpaid.
  2. Ask the Collections Office for a payoff and for the status of any lien.
  3. Tell your lender if taxes are escrowed so they are not paid twice.
  4. Give the title company a payoff request well before closing.

If the house is behind on tax, needs repair or both, selling as is for cash can clear the balance from the proceeds at settlement. Call or text us with the address and we will tell you what we can offer.

faqs.q: What is the Carroll County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The county rate is $1.018 per $100 of assessed value, plus $0.112 for the state, for $1.130 per $100 outside a town. Town rates are added where they apply.

faqs.q: Which Carroll County town has the highest total rate?
faqs.a: Westminster, at $1.6900 per $100 combined. Mount Airy has the lowest town total at $1.3262.

faqs.q: Is there a discount for paying Carroll County tax early?
faqs.a: Yes, for full-year payments only: 1% by July 31 and 0.5% by August 31. Semi-annual payments get no discount.

faqs.q: When is the Carroll County tax sale?
faqs.a: It is held online each June. From May 1, cash, certified check or money order is required.

faqs.q: How much did Carroll County assessments rise in 2026?
faqs.a: Residential full cash value rose 16.1% from January 1, 2023 to January 1, 2026. Increases phase in over three years.
